pass_a_gloss:
You take counsel, lift up a vain comfort. The amnesty for those who have been provoked is promised, and it is said that God will not be overly bitter towards them, having taken good counsel. But they consider the vain comfort to be a great and lofty thing, and they are carried away beyond what is reasonable. What is the great comfort they consider, which is also useless? That one, certainly. For they say, 'We will make a covenant with Hades and a pact with death.' If a tempest comes, it will not come to us. We have made a lie our hope, and we will be covered by the lie. But those who think these things and have a vain hope, thinking they will die before the terrible things they hear, will be trampled by the tempest when it comes. When it passes, it will seize you. Woe to the city of Ariel, which David besieged. Gather your harvest year after year. You will eat with Moab. I will destroy Ariel, and its strength and wealth will be, and I will surround it, as David did to you. I will put a siege around you and set up towers against you, and your words will be humbled to the ground, and your words will fall to the ground. Your voice will be like one calling from the earth, and your voice will be weak towards the ground.

For types of the true things happened to the ancients as in shadows. Now Jerusalem was once called Jebus. The blessed David captured it. And for what reason, we will come from the holy Scriptures. For it has thus in the second book of Kings: And David went, and all his men, to Jerusalem against the Jebusite who dwelled in the land, and it was said to David, 'David will not come here,' because the blind and the lame rose up saying, 'He will not come here.' And David captured the stronghold of Zion. This is the city of David. And David said on that day, 'Whoever strikes a Jebusite, let him strike the blind and the lame with the sword, the soul of David.' Therefore, the blessed David was opposed by the blind and the lame from Jerusalem or Jebus, and they were miserably destroyed. For he captured it, but the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the blind and the lame, opposed the Savior Christ at the time of his visit, for they did not know how to walk uprightly. But they also did not accept the divine light into their mind…
pass_b_english: You take counsel and lift up a vain comfort, promising amnesty to those who have been provoked and saying that God will not be overly bitter toward them, having taken good counsel.
Yet you regard this vain comfort as something great and lofty, and so you are carried away beyond what is reasonable.

What is this great and useless comfort you consider? It is this: 'We will make a covenant with Hades and a pact with death; if a tempest comes, it will not come to us; we have made a lie our hope, and we will be sheltered by the lie.' (Isaiah 28:15)

But those who entertain these thoughts and cling to empty hope, imagining they will die before the terrible things they hear, will hear clearly: 'When the tempest comes, you will become a trampling for it. When it passes, it will seize you.' (Isaiah 28:18-19)
Woe to the city of Ariel, which David besieged! (Isaiah 29:1)

Gather your harvest year after year, yet you shall eat with Moab, for I will lay waste to Ariel; her strength and wealth shall be mine, and I will encamp against you like David, raising fortifications and setting up towers. (Isaiah 29:2-3)
Then your speech will be brought low, speaking from the ground, and your utterance will bow down to the dust. (Isaiah 29:4)
Your voice shall be like that of one calling from the earth, and your voice shall be weak towards the ground. (Isaiah 29:4)
Now Jerusalem was once called Jebus, and the blessed David captured it. (2 Samuel 5:6-7)

David went with all his men to Jerusalem against the Jebusite inhabitant of the land, and it was said to him: 'You shall not enter here,' because the blind and the lame had taken their stand, saying, 'He shall not enter here.' (2 Samuel 5:6)
Nevertheless, David captured the stronghold of Zion, which became the city of David. (2 Samuel 5:7)
On that day David declared: 'Whoever attacks a Jebusite, let him strike the blind and the lame with the sword, the soul of David.' (2 Samuel 5:8)
Thus the blessed David was opposed by the blind and the lame from Jerusalem or Jebus, and they were miserably overthrown.

He captured the city, yet later the inhabitants of Jerusalem—the blind and the lame—opposed the Savior Christ at the time of his visitation, because they did not know how to walk uprightly, nor did they receive the divine light into their mind…
